tools.name: general
tools.description: Handles greetings, small talk directed at the assistant, and questions about what this assistant can do. Not a clinical or administrative tool — just conversational framing around the assistant itself.
use_when: User greets the assistant (e.g. hello, hi, good morning).
User asks what the assistant can do, how to use it, or what it's for.
User makes small talk directed at the assistant itself.
User thanks the assistant or says goodbye.
do_not_use_when: User wants a prediction, guideline, procedure, triage, appointment, or policy answer.
User asks something unrelated to this hospital assistant entirely.

tools.name: readmission_risk
tools.description: Predicts the probability that a patient will be readmitted to the hospital within a specified time window (e.g., 30 days) using structured clinical data.
use_when: User asks about readmission risk.
User wants a readmission prediction.
User provides patient clinical features for readmission estimation.
User asks whether a patient is likely to return to the hospital.
examples: Predict readmission risk for this patient.
Will this patient likely be readmitted?

tools.name: high_risk_patients
tools.description: Identifies whether a patient belongs to a high-risk clinical category based on available patient information.
use_when: User asks if a patient is high risk.
User wants patient risk stratification.
User asks to identify high-risk patients.
do_not_use_when: User asks specifically about readmission prediction.
examples: Classify this patient into risk categories.

tools.name: health_guidelines
tools.description: Retrieves evidence-based medical guidelines, recommendations, best practices, and clinical protocols from trusted medical documents.
use_when: User asks for disease management guidelines.
User asks what clinical guidelines recommend.
User requests standard medical recommendations.
User asks about prevention or management recommendations.
do_not_use_when: User asks for a procedural workflow.
examples: What are the diabetes management guidelines?

tools.name: treatment_procedures
tools.description: Retrieves step-by-step treatment procedures, clinical workflows, operative procedures, and medical protocols.
use_when: User asks how a medical procedure is performed.
User requests treatment workflow.
User asks for procedural steps.
User asks about surgical or clinical procedures.
examples: Procedure for central venous catheter insertion.

tools.name: triage
tools.description: Assesses patient symptoms and determines the urgency or priority of medical attention.
use_when: User describes symptoms.
User asks whether immediate medical care is needed.
User wants urgency assessment.
User requests emergency prioritization.
examples: I have chest pain. What should I do?
My child has a fever and breathing difficulty.
Should I go to the emergency room?

tools.name: appointment
tools.description: Handles appointment-related tasks such as booking, rescheduling, cancelling, or checking appointment availability.
use_when: User wants to book an appointment.
User wants to reschedule.
User wants to cancel.
User asks about appointment availability.

tools.name: policy_search
tools.description: Searches hospital or organizational policies, administrative rules, insurance policies, and operational documentation.
use_when: User asks about hospital policies.
User asks insurance coverage rules.
User asks administrative procedures.
User asks organizational regulations.

tools.name: unknown
tools.description: Use only when the request is unrelated to this hospital assistant's supported capabilities altogether. Do NOT use this for greetings or 'what can you do' questions — those go to 'general'.
use_when: The request is unrelated to healthcare or to this assistant's capabilities.
No tool, including 'general', has a clear match.
Multiple tools partially match but none confidently.
do_not_use_when: The user is greeting the assistant or asking what it can do (use 'general' instead).
examples: Who won the football match yesterday?
